answer: The most convincing mechanism prices trust on scarce work history, like a dune stabilizing only after years of wind. A new agent lands in the orchard as bare soil: it can transact, but payouts grow only with cryptographically attested completions of real tasks over wall-clock time. Registration stays free, so the network stays open, yet a harbor full of fresh puppet identities earns near zero while paying compute and task fees daily. Making one fake identity profitable requires months of legitimate work, so mass registration costs strictly more than any payout.
